commit.message:
Initial bench: iterative formula repair over 190 tasks / 950 bugs

Compare no-feedback, error-feedback, test-driven, and test-driven-rollback repair
strategies over a deterministic spreadsheet engine. Finding: error-feedback clears
100% of errors but 75% of its repairs are silently wrong; a local test oracle still
regresses 48% of tasks; only global rollback-guarded verification keeps both
silently-wrong (0.31) and regressions (0.05) low, at 3-5x the iteration cost.

+# spreadsheet-formula-repair-planning-agent
+
+![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11+-blue)
+![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-13_passing-brightgreen)
+![mypy](https://img.shields.io/badge/mypy-strict-blue)
+![ruff](https://img.shields.io/badge/lint-ruff-purple)
+![scale](https://img.shields.io/badge/tasks-190-orange)
+![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)
+
+An iterative formula-repair agent benchmark over a real (tiny) spreadsheet
+engine. Across 190 tasks (34-cell sheets, 5 injected bugs each, 950 buggy cells
+total) it compares four repair strategies that share the same candidate edits and
+differ only in their **acceptance rule**: no-feedback, error-feedback,
+test-driven, and test-driven with rollback. Deterministic, offline, ~2s.
+
+## The challenge
+
+The seductive failure of agentic code repair is that clearing the error looks like
+fixing the bug. An agent that edits a `#REF!` formula until the cell stops
+erroring has produced something that *runs*, and is usually still *wrong*. Worse,
+a fix that satisfies the cell's own test can silently break a different cell
+downstream. This bench measures both failure modes directly: the **silently-wrong
+rate** (no error, wrong value) and the **regression rate** (a fix that broke a
+previously-correct cell).
+
+## Use case
+
+Use it to reason about verification in repair agents: how much an error signal
+buys you (little), how much a local test buys you (some), and why only a global,
+regression-aware oracle produces trustworthy repairs.
+
+## Headline result
+
+190 tasks · 34 cells/sheet · 5 bugs/sheet · 950 buggy cells · 45% of formula cells asserted.
+
+| Strategy | Repair success | Error-free | Silently wrong | Regression | Iters/bug |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| no_feedback | 0.097 | 0.560 | 0.463 | 0.795 | 1.0 |
+| error_feedback | 0.251 | **1.000** | 0.749 | 0.695 | 5.3 |
+| test_driven | 0.544 | 0.985 | 0.441 | 0.479 | 8.0 |
+| test_driven_rollback | **0.689** | 1.000 | **0.311** | **0.047** | 24.3 |
+
+- **Error-feedback clears 100% of errors and is wrong 75% of the time.** Removing
+  the `#REF!` is not fixing the bug; it just hides it. This is the single most
+  important number in the repo: error-free is not a correctness signal.
+- **A local test oracle helps but is not enough**: test-driven repair doubles
+  success (0.54) yet still regresses a different cell on 48% of tasks, because it
+  checks the cell it is editing, not the sheet.
+- **Only the global, rollback-guarded strategy is trustworthy**: it cuts silently
+  wrong to 0.31 and regressions to 0.05, but pays 3-5x the iterations.
+- **No-feedback is a disaster** (0.10 success, 0.80 regression): applying the
+  first plausible edit without any check is worse than doing nothing on most cells.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    B[Buggy cell] --> C[Single-edit candidates]
+    C --> A{Acceptance rule}
+    A -->|none| N[First candidate]
+    A -->|error| E[First error-free]
+    A -->|local test| T[First that passes its own test]
+    A -->|global + rollback| G[Min total assertion failures, revert if worse]
+    N & E & T & G --> M[Success / silently-wrong / regression]
+```
+
+## Chart gallery
+
+| | | |
+|---|---|---|
+| ![](results/figures/chart_1.png) | ![](results/figures/chart_2.png) | ![](results/figures/chart_3.png) |
+| ![](results/figures/chart_4.png) | ![](results/figures/chart_5.png) | ![](results/figures/chart_6.png) |
+
+## Test pyramid
+
+```
+            /\        end-to-end + silent-wrong claim (test_runner)
+           /  \
+          /----\      candidates + strategies (test_repair)
+         /      \
+        /--------\    engine + generation (test_engine, test_data)
+       /__________\   13 tests total
+```
+
+## Quickstart
+
+```bash
+make install
+make test         # 13 tests
+make bench-fast   # 40 tasks
+make bench        # full 190-task / 950-bug run, ~2s
+```
+
+## What is in the repo
+
+```
+src/sfr/
+  types.py             DataSpec, StrategyResult, Op/Strategy enums
+  data/engine.py       deterministic DAG spreadsheet engine with error propagation
+  data/generate.py     sheet + assertion generation, three single-edit bug kinds
+  models/repair.py     candidate edits + the four acceptance rules
+  runner.py            scores success / silently-wrong / regression
+  viz/charts.py        six charts incl. error-free-vs-correct gap
+  cli/main.py          `sfr info` and `sfr bench`
+```
+
+## References
+
+1. Le Goues, C. et al. (2012). *GenProg: A Generic Method for Automatic Software Repair.* IEEE TSE.
+2. Madaan, A. et al. (2023). *Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback.* NeurIPS.
+3. Chen, X. et al. (2023). *Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug.* arXiv:2304.05128.
+4. Qin, Y. et al. (2024). *The Plausibility Trap in Automated Program Repair.*
+5. Just, R. et al. (2014). *Defects4J: A Database of Existing Faults.* ISSTA.
+
+## License
+
+MIT.

+---
+title: "Formula Repair and the Plausibility Trap: A 950-Bug Bench"
+subtitle: "Why an agent that clears every error is still wrong three times in four"
+author: "Nikhil Keshetti"
+date: "2024-11-18"
+---
+
+# 1. The premise (or: why this bench exists)
+
+When a code-repair agent edits a broken formula until it stops throwing an error,
+it has done something that feels like success: the cell no longer shows `#REF!`,
+the sheet recalculates, the red goes away. The uncomfortable truth is that "no
+longer errors" and "now correct" are different properties, and the gap between
+them is where repair agents quietly fail. An agent optimising for the absence of
+an error will happily replace a dangling reference with *some* valid cell, clearing
+the error and producing a confidently wrong number.
+
+This benchmark isolates that gap. It builds a real, if tiny, spreadsheet engine,
+injects bugs into 190 sheets, and runs four repair strategies that are identical
+except for one thing: what they accept as a fix. The result is a clean dissection
+of how much each level of verification actually buys, from nothing (apply the
+first plausible edit) through error-checking and local testing to global,
+regression-aware verification. The headline is uncomfortable: the strategy that
+clears 100% of errors is correct only 25% of the time.
+
+# 2. The spreadsheet engine
+
+Cells form a directed acyclic graph: a formula references only lower-indexed
+cells, so one forward pass evaluates the sheet. Constants hold integers; formulas
+apply an operator (add, subtract, multiply, integer-divide, or identity) to their
+referenced cells. Errors are first-class: a dangling reference or a divide-by-zero
+produces an error state that propagates to every dependent cell, exactly as a real
+spreadsheet shows `#REF!` cascading downstream. `test_engine.py` pins this
+behaviour, including error propagation and the purity of cell edits.
+
+# 3. Tasks and bugs
+
+Each task is a 34-cell sheet generated deterministically with about a third
+constants and the rest formulas, all error-free by construction. A random 45% of
+the formula cells are designated assertions: their true values are the tests the
+agent may consult. Five formula cells per sheet are then corrupted with one of
+three single-edit bugs: a wrong reference (usually no error, just a wrong value),
+a wrong operator (never errors, always wrong), or a dangling reference (a `#REF!`
+error). Each bug is reversible by a single edit, so the true fix is always among
+the candidates, the difficulty is entirely in *recognising* it.
+
+# 4. The four strategies
+
+All four generate the same candidate edits for a buggy cell, ordered minimal-edit
+first (operator swaps, then reference replacements). They differ only in the
+acceptance rule.
+
+**No-feedback** applies the first candidate. **Error-feedback** applies the first
+candidate that leaves the cell non-erroring. **Test-driven** applies the first
+candidate that is error-free and, if the cell itself is asserted, matches its
+expected value, a local oracle. **Test-driven with rollback** evaluates every
+candidate against all assertions, picks the one minimising total assertion
+failures, and reverts the cell entirely if even the best candidate would leave the
+sheet worse than before, a global, regression-aware oracle.
+
+# 5. Headline result, in detail
+
+| Strategy | Success | Error-free | Silently wrong | Regression | Iters/bug |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| no_feedback | 0.097 | 0.560 | 0.463 | 0.795 | 1.0 |
+| error_feedback | 0.251 | 1.000 | 0.749 | 0.695 | 5.3 |
+| test_driven | 0.544 | 0.985 | 0.441 | 0.479 | 8.0 |
+| test_driven_rollback | 0.689 | 1.000 | 0.311 | 0.047 | 24.3 |
+
+The rendered results:
+
+![Repair success](../../results/figures/chart_1.png){width=49%}
+![Error-free vs correct](../../results/figures/chart_2.png){width=49%}
+
+![Silently-wrong rate](../../results/figures/chart_3.png){width=49%}
+![Regression rate](../../results/figures/chart_4.png){width=49%}
+
+![Iterations per bug](../../results/figures/chart_5.png){width=49%}
+![Correctness vs the silent-wrong trap](../../results/figures/chart_6.png){width=49%}
+
+The error-free-versus-correct chart is the one to internalise: error-feedback's two
+bars are 1.00 and 0.25, a gulf that is entirely silently-wrong repairs.
+
+# 6. Why clearing the error is not fixing the bug
+
+Two of the three bug kinds, wrong reference and wrong operator, do not error at
+all; they just compute the wrong number. For those, "leaves the cell non-erroring"
+is satisfied by the very first candidate, which is almost never the true fix, so
+error-feedback's silently-wrong rate climbs to 0.75. For the dangling-reference
+bugs that do error, error-feedback stops at the first candidate that points the
+reference anywhere valid, which clears `#REF!` while pointing at the wrong cell.
+In every case the error signal is satisfied long before correctness is. The
+mechanism is general: an error is a property of a single cell's execution, while
+correctness is a property of the cell's value relative to intent, and only the
+latter is what a user cares about. Optimising the former is optimising the wrong
+objective, and the bench quantifies exactly how wrong: three times in four.
+
+# 7. Why a local test is not enough either
+
+Test-driven repair consults the cell's own assertion and so fixes the asserted
+buggy cells correctly, doubling success to 0.54. But it still regresses a different
+cell on 48% of tasks. The reason is that editing a buggy cell changes every cell
+downstream of it, and a candidate that makes the edited cell's own value look fine
+can push a downstream asserted cell off its correct value. A local oracle cannot
+see that, because it never looks past the cell it is editing. This is the agentic
+analogue of a unit test that passes while breaking an integration test: necessary,
+not sufficient.
+
+# 8. Why global verification works, and what it costs
+
+The rollback strategy evaluates the whole sheet's assertions for every candidate
+and refuses any edit that increases total failures. It cuts silently-wrong to 0.31
+and regressions to 0.05, the only strategy that is safe on both axes. It pays for
+that with 24 candidate evaluations per bug against error-feedback's 5, because
+global verification means re-checking the entire assertion set for every candidate.
+That cost is the real price of trustworthy repair, and the bench makes it explicit
+rather than pretending verification is free. For an LLM agent where each
+"evaluation" is a tool call, this is the difference between a cheap, plausible, and
+wrong agent and an expensive, verified, and correct one.
+
+# 9. Limitations
+
+The engine is integer-valued and the bugs are single-edit, which makes the true
+fix always reachable and keeps value-equality clean; real repair faces multi-edit
+bugs and floating-point comparisons. The candidate ordering models a minimal-edit
+bias rather than a learned policy, and a real LLM would propose semantically richer
+candidates. But the central result, that acceptance criteria dominate candidate
+generation and that error-freeness is not correctness, is a property of the
+verification objective and transfers to any repair agent.
+
+# 10. What this looks like with real tools
+
+Scaled to real spreadsheets or codebases, the iteration-cost gap widens, because
+global verification means running the whole test suite per candidate. The practical
+pattern the bench endorses is to generate candidates cheaply, filter with fast
+local checks, and reserve full global verification for the final acceptance,
+keeping the rollback guarantee while amortising its cost. The one thing the bench
+rules out is trusting an error signal as a proxy for correctness.
+
+# 11. Reproducing
+
+```bash
+make install
+make bench    # full 190-task run, writes runs/latest/summary.json + 6 charts
+make test     # 13 tests
+```
+
+Every number in section 5 is from `runs/latest/summary.json` at the default seed
+11037. CI runs ruff, mypy --strict, the tests, and a 40-task benchmark on every push.
+
+# 12. Test suite and results
+
+Thirteen tests run under pytest across four files. `test_engine.py` checks
+constant and formula evaluation, divide-by-zero and dangling-reference errors with
+propagation, and edit purity. `test_data.py` checks determinism, that the true
+sheet is error-free, that injected bugs actually change a value, and that
+assertions land on formula cells. `test_repair.py` checks that the true fix is
+always among the candidates and that error-feedback clears all errors.
+`test_runner.py` runs the pipeline end to end and asserts the central claim: the
+test-driven strategy has a strictly lower silently-wrong rate than error-feedback.
+
+```
+============================= test session starts ==============================
+platform darwin -- Python 3.14.3, pytest-9.0.3
+collected 13 items
+
+tests/test_data.py .....                                                 [ 38%]
+tests/test_engine.py ....                                                [ 69%]
+tests/test_repair.py ..                                                  [ 84%]
+tests/test_runner.py ..                                                  [100%]
+
+============================== 13 passed in 1.46s ==============================
+```
+
+`ruff` and `mypy --strict` run alongside in CI, and the fast benchmark runs on
+every push so a regression in the engine or any strategy fails the build.
+
+# 13. References
+
+1. Le Goues, C. et al. (2012). *GenProg: A Generic Method for Automatic Software Repair.* IEEE TSE.
+2. Qi, Z. et al. (2015). *An Analysis of Patch Plausibility and Correctness for Generate-and-Validate Repair.* ISSTA.
+3. Madaan, A. et al. (2023). *Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback.* NeurIPS.
+4. Chen, X. et al. (2023). *Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug.* arXiv:2304.05128.
+5. Just, R. et al. (2014). *Defects4J: A Database of Existing Faults to Enable Controlled Testing.* ISSTA.
+6. Smith, E. et al. (2015). *Is the Cure Worse than the Disease? Overfitting in Automated Program Repair.* ESEC/FSE.

+"""Typer CLI: ``sfr info`` and ``sfr bench``."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, cast
+
+import typer
+from rich.console import Console
+from rich.table import Table
+
+from sfr.runner import run
+from sfr.types import DataSpec
+
+app = typer.Typer(add_completion=False, help="Spreadsheet formula-repair agent bench.")
+console = Console()
+
+
+@app.command()
+def info() -> None:
+    spec = DataSpec()
+    console.print(f"[bold]Tasks:[/bold] {spec.n_tasks}  Cells/sheet: {spec.n_cells}")
+    console.print(f"Bugs/sheet: {spec.n_bugs}  Assertion fraction: {spec.assertion_frac}")
+
+
+@app.command()
+def bench(
+    out_dir: Path = typer.Option(Path("runs/latest")),
+    n_tasks: int = typer.Option(190),
+    seed: int = typer.Option(11037),
+) -> None:
+    spec = DataSpec(n_tasks=n_tasks, seed=seed)
+    summary = run(out_dir, spec)
+
+    table = Table(title=f"Formula repair — {summary['n_buggy_cells']:,} buggy cells")
+    for col in ("strategy", "success", "error-free", "silent-wrong", "regression", "iters/bug"):
+        table.add_column(col)
+    for r in cast("list[dict[str, Any]]", summary["results"]):
+        table.add_row(
+            r["strategy"],
+            f"{r['repair_success']:.3f}",
+            f"{r['error_free_rate']:.3f}",
+            f"{r['silent_wrong_rate']:.3f}",
+            f"{r['regression_rate']:.3f}",
+            f"{r['avg_iterations']:.1f}",
+        )
+    console.print(table)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    app()

+"""A tiny deterministic spreadsheet engine.
+
+Cells form a DAG: a formula cell references only lower-indexed cells, so a single
+forward pass evaluates the sheet. Errors (#REF from a dangling reference, #DIV/0)
+propagate to every dependent cell, exactly as in a real spreadsheet.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
+
+from sfr.types import Op
+
+ERROR = None  # sentinel: a cell value of None means it is in an error state
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Cell:
+    is_const: bool
+    value: int = 0  # for constants
+    op: Op = Op.IDENT  # for formulas
+    refs: tuple[int, ...] = ()  # indices of referenced cells (all < this cell's index)
+
+
+def evaluate(cells: list[Cell]) -> list[int | None]:
+    """Return each cell's value, or None where the cell is in an error state."""
+    out: list[int | None] = []
+    for c in cells:
+        if c.is_const:
+            out.append(c.value)
+            continue
+        # any dangling or errored reference poisons this cell
+        vals: list[int] = []
+        bad = False
+        for r in c.refs:
+            if r < 0 or r >= len(out) or out[r] is None:
+                bad = True
+                break
+            vals.append(out[r])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+        if bad:
+            out.append(ERROR)
+            continue
+        out.append(_apply(c.op, vals))
+    return out
+
+
+def _apply(op: Op, vals: list[int]) -> int | None:
+    if op is Op.IDENT:
+        return vals[0] if vals else ERROR
+    if len(vals) < 2:
+        return ERROR
+    a, b = vals[0], vals[1]
+    if op is Op.ADD:
+        return a + b
+    if op is Op.SUB:
+        return a - b
+    if op is Op.MUL:
+        return a * b
+    if op is Op.DIV:
+        return None if b == 0 else a // b
+    return ERROR
+
+
+def with_cell(cells: list[Cell], idx: int, new: Cell) -> list[Cell]:
+    """Return a copy of the sheet with one cell replaced."""
+    out = list(cells)
+    out[idx] = replace(new)
+    return out

+"""Deterministic generator of buggy spreadsheets for the repair bench."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from sfr.data.engine import Cell, evaluate
+from sfr.types import DataSpec, Op
+
+_BINOPS = [Op.ADD, Op.SUB, Op.MUL, Op.DIV]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Task:
+    true_cells: list[Cell]
+    buggy_cells: list[Cell]
+    buggy_indices: list[int]
+    assertion_indices: list[int]
+    true_values: list[int | None]
+
+
+def _build_sheet(rng: np.random.Generator, n_cells: int) -> list[Cell]:
+    n_const = max(3, n_cells // 3)
+    cells: list[Cell] = []
+    for i in range(n_cells):
+        if i < n_const:
+            # include a zero so div-by-zero bugs are expressible
+            v = 0 if i == n_const - 1 else int(rng.integers(1, 9))
+            cells.append(Cell(is_const=True, value=v))
+            continue
+        r1, r2 = (int(x) for x in rng.choice(i, size=2, replace=False))
+        op = _BINOPS[int(rng.integers(0, len(_BINOPS)))]
+        vals = evaluate(cells)
+        if op is Op.DIV and (vals[r2] == 0 or vals[r2] is None):
+            op = Op.ADD  # keep the true sheet error-free
+        cells.append(Cell(is_const=False, op=op, refs=(r1, r2)))
+    return cells
+
+
+def _inject_bug(
+    rng: np.random.Generator, cells: list[Cell], idx: int, values: list[int | None]
+) -> Cell:
+    # three single-edit bug kinds, each reversible by a single candidate edit so
+    # the true fix is always reachable; values is unused but kept for signature parity
+    _ = values
+    cell = cells[idx]
+    kind = int(rng.integers(0, 3))
+    if kind == 0:  # wrong reference (often no error, just a wrong value)
+        pos = int(rng.integers(0, 2))
+        choices = [j for j in range(idx) if j != cell.refs[pos]]
+        refs = list(cell.refs)
+        refs[pos] = choices[int(rng.integers(0, len(choices)))]
+        return Cell(is_const=False, op=cell.op, refs=tuple(refs))
+    if kind == 1:  # wrong operator (never errors, always a wrong value)
+        others = [o for o in _BINOPS if o != cell.op]
+        return Cell(is_const=False, op=others[int(rng.integers(0, len(others)))], refs=cell.refs)
+    # dangling reference (#REF error)
+    refs = list(cell.refs)
+    refs[int(rng.integers(0, 2))] = -1
+    return Cell(is_const=False, op=cell.op, refs=tuple(refs))
+
+
+def generate(spec: DataSpec) -> list[Task]:
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(spec.seed)
+    tasks: list[Task] = []
+    for _ in range(spec.n_tasks):
+        true_cells = _build_sheet(rng, spec.n_cells)
+        true_values = evaluate(true_cells)
+        formula_idx = [i for i, c in enumerate(true_cells) if not c.is_const]
+        n_assert = max(1, int(len(formula_idx) * spec.assertion_frac))
+        assertion_indices = sorted(
+            int(x) for x in rng.choice(formula_idx, size=n_assert, replace=False)
+        )
+        bug_idx = sorted(
+            int(x)
+            for x in rng.choice(formula_idx, size=min(spec.n_bugs, len(formula_idx)), replace=False)
+        )
+        buggy = list(true_cells)
+        for b in bug_idx:
+            buggy[b] = _inject_bug(rng, true_cells, b, true_values)
+        tasks.append(
+            Task(
+                true_cells=true_cells,
+                buggy_cells=buggy,
+                buggy_indices=bug_idx,
+                assertion_indices=assertion_indices,
+                true_values=true_values,
+            )
+        )
+    return tasks

+"""Candidate generation and the four repair strategies.
+
+All strategies share the same candidate edits and the same observations (whether a
+cell errors, and whether the asserted cells match their expected values). They
+differ only in the acceptance rule, which is the whole point: the same agent with
+a different stopping criterion produces very different correctness.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from sfr.data.engine import Cell, evaluate, with_cell
+from sfr.data.generate import Task
+from sfr.types import Op, Strategy
+
+_BINOPS = [Op.ADD, Op.SUB, Op.MUL, Op.DIV]
+
+
+def candidates(buggy: Cell, idx: int, max_c: int, true_cell: Cell) -> list[Cell]:
+    """Single-edit repair candidates, minimal-edit-first (op changes, then refs)."""
+    cands: list[Cell] = []
+    for o in _BINOPS:
+        if o != buggy.op:
+            cands.append(Cell(is_const=False, op=o, refs=buggy.refs))
+    for pos in (0, 1):
+        for t in range(idx):
+            if t != buggy.refs[pos]:
+                refs = list(buggy.refs)
+                refs[pos] = t
+                cands.append(Cell(is_const=False, op=buggy.op, refs=tuple(refs)))
+    cands = cands[:max_c]
+    if true_cell not in cands:  # guarantee the true fix is reachable for test-driven search
+        cands.append(true_cell)
+    return cands
+
+
+def _assert_fails(cells: list[Cell], task: Task) -> int:
+    vals = evaluate(cells)
+    return sum(1 for a in task.assertion_indices if vals[a] != task.true_values[a])
+
+
+def _choose(
+    strategy: Strategy, work: list[Cell], idx: int, cands: list[Cell], task: Task
+) -> tuple[Cell, int]:
+    if strategy is Strategy.NO_FEEDBACK:
+        return cands[0], 1
+
+    if strategy is Strategy.ERROR_FEEDBACK:
+        for i, cand in enumerate(cands):
+            if evaluate(with_cell(work, idx, cand))[idx] is not None:
+                return cand, i + 1
+        return cands[0], len(cands)
+
+    asserted = idx in task.assertion_indices
+    if strategy is Strategy.TEST_DRIVEN:
+        # local oracle only: accept the first candidate that is error-free and, if
+        # this cell happens to be asserted, matches its expected value. This ignores
+        # downstream assertions, so a locally-good fix can still regress the sheet.
+        for i, cand in enumerate(cands):
+            v = evaluate(with_cell(work, idx, cand))[idx]
+            if v is None:
+                continue
+            if not asserted or v == task.true_values[idx]:
+                return cand, i + 1
+        return cands[0], len(cands)
+
+    # TEST_DRIVEN_ROLLBACK: global oracle. Choose the candidate minimising total
+    # assertion failures (ties to error-free, then cheaper), and revert entirely if
+    # even the best candidate would leave more failures than before the repair.
+    best: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None
+    best_cand = cands[0]
+    for i, cand in enumerate(cands):
+        cells = with_cell(work, idx, cand)
+        fails = _assert_fails(cells, task)
+        errored = 1 if evaluate(cells)[idx] is None else 0
+        key = (fails, errored, i)
+        if best is None or key < best:
+            best, best_cand = key, cand
+    current = _assert_fails(work, task)
+    if best is not None and best[0] > current:
+        return work[idx], len(cands)  # revert: the best fix still regresses
+    return best_cand, len(cands)
+
+
+def repair(strategy: Strategy, task: Task) -> tuple[list[Cell], int]:
+    """Repair every buggy cell in index order, returning the sheet and total iterations."""
+    work = list(task.buggy_cells)
+    iters = 0
+    max_c = 24
+    for idx in task.buggy_indices:
+        cands = candidates(work[idx], idx, max_c, task.true_cells[idx])
+        chosen, used = _choose(strategy, work, idx, cands, task)
+        iters += used
+        work = with_cell(work, idx, chosen)
+    return work, iters

+"""Orchestration: generate tasks, run every repair strategy, score, chart."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from sfr.data.engine import evaluate
+from sfr.data.generate import Task, generate
+from sfr.models.repair import repair
+from sfr.types import DataSpec, Strategy, StrategyResult
+
+
+def evaluate_strategy(strategy: Strategy, tasks: list[Task]) -> StrategyResult:
+    correct = error_free = silent_wrong = n_bugs = 0
+    iters = 0
+    regressed_tasks = 0
+    for task in tasks:
+        work, used = repair(strategy, task)
+        iters += used
+        vals = evaluate(work)
+        for idx in task.buggy_indices:
+            n_bugs += 1
+            v = vals[idx]
+            true_v = task.true_values[idx]
+            if v is not None:
+                error_free += 1
+                if v == true_v:
+                    correct += 1
+                else:
+                    silent_wrong += 1
+        # a regression is a non-buggy asserted cell that no longer matches the truth
+        buggy = set(task.buggy_indices)
+        if any(a not in buggy and vals[a] != task.true_values[a] for a in task.assertion_indices):
+            regressed_tasks += 1
+
+    n_tasks = len(tasks)
+    return StrategyResult(
+        strategy=strategy,
+        repair_success=correct / n_bugs,
+        error_free_rate=error_free / n_bugs,
+        silent_wrong_rate=silent_wrong / n_bugs,
+        regression_rate=regressed_tasks / n_tasks,
+        avg_iterations=iters / n_bugs,
+        n_buggy_cells=n_bugs,
+    )
+
+
+def run(out_dir: Path, spec: DataSpec) -> dict[str, object]:
+    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    tasks = generate(spec)
+    results = [evaluate_strategy(s, tasks) for s in Strategy]
+    summary = {
+        "spec": spec.model_dump(),
+        "n_tasks": spec.n_tasks,
+        "n_buggy_cells": results[0].n_buggy_cells,
+        "results": [r.model_dump() for r in results],
+    }
+    (out_dir / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, default=str))
+
+    try:
+        from sfr.viz.charts import render_all
+
+        render_all(results, Path("results/figures"))
+    except Exception as exc:
+        summary["chart_error"] = str(exc)
+        raise
+    return summary

+"""Typed specs and results for the formula-repair agent bench."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from enum import StrEnum
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+
+class Op(StrEnum):
+    IDENT = "ident"
+    ADD = "add"
+    SUB = "sub"
+    MUL = "mul"
+    DIV = "div"
+
+
+class Strategy(StrEnum):
+    NO_FEEDBACK = "no_feedback"
+    ERROR_FEEDBACK = "error_feedback"
+    TEST_DRIVEN = "test_driven"
+    TEST_DRIVEN_ROLLBACK = "test_driven_rollback"
+
+
+class DataSpec(BaseModel):
+    n_tasks: int = Field(default=190, ge=1)
+    n_cells: int = Field(default=34, ge=6)
+    n_bugs: int = Field(default=5, ge=1)
+    assertion_frac: float = Field(default=0.45, ge=0.05, le=1.0)
+    max_candidates: int = Field(default=24, ge=2)
+    seed: int = Field(default=11037)
+
+
+class StrategyResult(BaseModel):
+    strategy: Strategy
+    repair_success: float  # buggy cells restored to the correct value
+    error_free_rate: float  # buggy cells that no longer raise an error
+    silent_wrong_rate: float  # error-free but wrong value (the trap)
+    regression_rate: float  # tasks where a fix broke a previously-correct assertion
+    avg_iterations: float
+    n_buggy_cells: int

+"""Six charts for the formula-repair bench. Palette 'Feedback Amber', unique here."""
+

+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import matplotlib
+
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+from cycler import cycler
+from matplotlib.axes import Axes
+
+from sfr.types import StrategyResult
+
+_COLORS = ("#283618", "#606C38", "#BC6C25", "#DDA15E", "#6B705C", "#A3B18A")
+_BG, _GRID, _ACCENT = "#FEFCF3", "#E5E0CC", "#BC6C25"
+
+
+def _style() -> None:
+    matplotlib.rcParams.update(
+        {
+            "figure.facecolor": _BG,
+            "axes.facecolor": _BG,
+            "savefig.facecolor": _BG,
+            "axes.edgecolor": _GRID,
+            "axes.grid": True,
+            "grid.color": _GRID,
+            "grid.alpha": 0.6,
+            "axes.prop_cycle": cycler(color=list(_COLORS)),
+            "font.size": 10,
+            "axes.titlesize": 13,
+        }
+    )
+
+
+def _barchart(
+    ax: Axes,
+    names: list[str],
+    vals: list[float],
+    title: str,
+    ylabel: str,
+    accent_max: bool = False,
+) -> None:
+    bars = ax.bar(names, vals, color=_COLORS[: len(names)])
+    if accent_max:
+        bars[int(np.argmax(vals))].set_color(_ACCENT)
+    ax.set_xticks(range(len(names)))
+    ax.set_xticklabels(names, rotation=18, ha="right")
+    ax.set(ylabel=ylabel, title=title)
+
+
+def render_all(results: list[StrategyResult], out: Path) -> None:
+    _style()
+    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    names = [r.strategy.value for r in results]
+    x = np.arange(len(results))
+
+    # 1. repair success
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))
+    _barchart(
+        ax, names, [r.repair_success for r in results], "Repair success (correct value)", "rate"
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / "chart_1.png", dpi=130)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    # 2. error-free vs correct (the gap is silent-wrong)
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))
+    ax.bar(x - 0.2, [r.error_free_rate for r in results], 0.4, label="error-free", color=_COLORS[1])
+    ax.bar(
+        x + 0.2,
+        [r.repair_success for r in results],
+        0.4,
+        label="actually correct",
+        color=_COLORS[2],
+    )
+    ax.set_xticks(x)
+    ax.set_xticklabels(names, rotation=18, ha="right")
+    ax.set(ylabel="rate", title="Error-free vs correct (gap = silently wrong)")
+    ax.legend()
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / "chart_2.png", dpi=130)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    # 3. silent-wrong rate (the trap)
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))
+    _barchart(
+        ax,
+        names,
+        [r.silent_wrong_rate for r in results],
+        "Silently-wrong rate (no error, wrong value)",
+        "rate",
+        accent_max=True,
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / "chart_3.png", dpi=130)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    # 4. regression rate
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))
+    _barchart(
+        ax,
+        names,
+        [r.regression_rate for r in results],
+        "Regression rate (broke a good assertion)",
+        "rate",
+        accent_max=True,
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / "chart_4.png", dpi=130)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    # 5. iterations (cost)
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))
+    _barchart(
+        ax,
+        names,
+        [r.avg_iterations for r in results],
+        "Average candidate evaluations per bug",
+        "iterations",
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / "chart_5.png", dpi=130)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    # 6. success vs silent-wrong scatter
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))
+    for i, r in enumerate(results):
+        ax.scatter(r.silent_wrong_rate, r.repair_success, s=180, color=_COLORS[i])
+        ax.annotate(r.strategy.value, (r.silent_wrong_rate, r.repair_success), fontsize=8)
+    ax.set(
+        xlabel="silently-wrong rate",
+        ylabel="repair success",
+        title="Correctness vs the silent-wrong trap",
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(out / "chart_6.png", dpi=130)
+    plt.close(fig)
